Marathon Petroleum ticked up less than 1% today, extending a strong two-week rally of nearly 9%. The modest gain follows a sharp pullback yesterday from a peak of $399.44, suggesting consolidation after this recent surge. The driver is clear: oil prices jumped on news that Saudi Arabia shut down a critical pipeline to bypass the Strait of Hormuz after escalating attacks from Iran-allied groups, raising concerns about supply disruptions in one of the world's most important oil chokepoints. Refiners like Marathon benefit when crude oil prices rise relative to the products they sell (gasoline and diesel), and with US oil now at $97.26 per barrel and refinery utilization running at 97.8%, the company is positioned to capture higher margins on that tighter supply backdrop.

The broader context is the escalating Iran-Gulf tensions, which have created sustained upward pressure on energy prices over the past week despite no actual supply loss yet. As long as the geopolitical risk premium persists and refineries run near full capacity, refiners have pricing power — though any actual pipeline repairs or diplomatic breakthrough could reverse these gains quickly.
